Her imaging was subsequently reviewed by a neuroradiologist specialising in vascular imaging. There was a suspicion of a right sigmoid VST given abnormal flow void on T2 sequences (see Figure 1(c)). panels.rationale: Single sagittal T2-weighted MRI of a real patient showing longitudinal cervical cord/medullary oedema and signal change; the caption explicitly states this could be an indirect finding suggesting a dural arteriovenous fistula, and the accompanying in-text description of the same figure reports prominent flow voids and engorged spinal veins, supporting attribution to intracranial dural AV fistula. Attribution is indirect (oedema/venous congestion rather than direct shunt depiction), hence moderate confidence.

panels.figure_caption: T2-weighted MRI scan showing the extent of spinal cord oedema (orange arrows) Signal change seen especially in the medulla and upper cervical cord (red arrow). This could be an indirect finding to suggest the presence of a dural arteriovenous fistula.

Computed tomography (CT) of his thorax, abdomen and pelvis was unremarkable. Some improvement in lower limb power was seen with cyclophosphamide and a reducing-regimen of oral prednisolone.
